name: app.apiguru/amazon-data
title: Apiguru Amazon Data
description: Live Amazon product, review, search, deal, offer/stock and seller data across 23 marketplaces.

tools.name: product_details
tools.description: Use for one product's current listing. Not for several ASINs (product_details_batch), seller offers or stock (offers_stock), or review text (product_reviews). Fetches the complete product record for one ASIN on one marketplace: title, price, star rating, rating count, images, description, feature bullets, variations and category. Price: $0.003 per call. 404 means the ASIN is absent from that marketplace and IS billed. 503 is a temporary failure on our side and is NOT billed - retry. Bullet points and specs are what Amazon shows for the listing; on multi-variant listings they can describe the product family rather than the exact variant. A null field means Amazon did not show it. Beside the price the record carries what the page shows there: `discount_percentage` (the saving against `product_original_price`, an integer), `product_price_per_unit` ("$0.59/fluid ounce"), `deal_badge` ("Limited time deal"), `coupon` and `promotion` in the page's own words, and `subscribe_and_save` -- `{price, price_per_unit, max_savings_price, max_savings_percentage}`, null when the listing has no such option. `return_policy` is the buy box's Returns line ("FREE refund/replacement until Jan 31, 2027"), and `buybox_winner.seller_url` is the seller's page. Three things a listing states are named at the top level: `whats_in_the_box` (the page's "What's in the box" list, an array of strings), `warranty` ("1 year manufacturer") and `ingredients` (the ingredient list as the page prints it); each is null when the listing states none. `product_information` still holds the same rows under the page's own labels. `product_photos` is this listing's whole gallery at full size, in the page's order (it used to hold one image, or thumbnails); other variants' images stay under `variation`. A page that comes back with no product on it is fetched again and, failing that, answered as the unbilled 503 -- never as an empty record. Keys of `product_information`, `tech_specs` and the other specification tables are trimmed: Amazon prints some rows twice, once with a trailing space ("Package Dimensions "), and the copies are merged under the clean name; when they differ the listing's own value wins (the second copy of "ASIN" on a variant often names the parent). `currency` is the symbol Amazon prints on the page ($, €, £, R$, AED); the ISO code is `price_snapshot.currency`. `is_best_seller` and `badges.best_seller` are true only for the listing's own "#1 Best Seller" badge. `ranks` and `category_path` are empty when Amazon's page for the listing shows no Best Sellers Rank rows or breadcrumb; a listing with the badge then gets one `ranks` entry read from the badge (rank 1 in the category the badge names), marked `source: best_seller_badge`.

asin.description: Single Amazon ASIN, 10 uppercase alphanumeric characters. Exactly one - comma-separated lists are rejected; use product_details_batch for many. An Amazon product URL (…/dp/ASIN) works too, in place of an ASIN; lower case is fine. A URL's domain sets the marketplace unless geo says otherwise.
asin.title: Asin

compact.description: Return the compact record (about 4 KB: identity, price with its discount, unit price, deal, coupon and Subscribe & Save, rating, availability, return policy, box contents, warranty, ingredients, bullets, category, offer, buy box). false returns the full record (about 75 KB, includes from_manufacturer, tech_specs, product_information, product_reviews).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated top-level fields to return instead of the compact set, e.g. "tech_specs,product_information". Any response lists what it left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: product_reviews
tools.description: Use for what customers say about one product. Not for its full review history (Amazon serves full and star-filtered review lists only to signed-in accounts) or for seller feedback (seller_reviews). Returns the overall rating, rating count, review_histogram (percent of all ratings per star), Amazon's 'customers say' AI summary where that marketplace shows one, and the reviews on the product page (typically up to 8 from this marketplace and 5 from other countries; none on amazon.com at present, where Amazon shows review text only to signed-in visitors), each with rating, review_date, review_country, from_this_marketplace, verified flag and helpful_votes; from_rating/to_rating keep a star window. Price: $0.003 per call. Same 404-billed / 503-not-billed semantics as product_details. No paging or sort: the reviews are those on the product page; review_coverage says how many and from where. from_rating/to_rating filter them. review_histogram (here and on product_details) gives the share of every rating. customers_say is null where Amazon shows no summary (several marketplaces never do); customers_say_note then says so. Where Amazon shows review text on the product page only to signed-in visitors (amazon.com at present), `product_reviews` is empty and `review_coverage.note` says so; the rating, rating count, review_histogram and customers_say are returned as usual.

asin.description: Single Amazon ASIN, 10 uppercase alphanumeric characters. An Amazon product URL (…/dp/ASIN) works too, in place of an ASIN; lower case is fine. A URL's domain sets the marketplace unless geo says otherwise.
asin.title: Asin

from_rating.description: Lowest star rating to include, 1-5. Filters the reviews the product page shows (see review_coverage).
from_rating.title: From Rating

to_rating.description: Highest star rating to include, 1-5. from_rating=1&to_rating=3 keeps the critical ones among them.
to_rating.title: To Rating

max_reviews.description: Cap on individual reviews returned (0 = all). The rating summary, review_histogram and customers_say are always returned; _reviews_total is the number of reviews on the product page (not all reviews; see review_coverage).
max_reviews.title: Max Reviews

tools.name: search
tools.description: Use to find products by keyword and filters. Rows are result snippets; for the authoritative record of one ASIN call product_details. Search Amazon products by keyword. Filters: page, sort_by, category_id (browse node), min_price / max_price (decimals), product_condition (NEW / USED / RENEWED), brand, seller_id, today_deals and deal_type (coupons, all_discounts, buy_more_save_more). Every answer carries filters_applied, filters_ignored (with the reason) and available_filters for that marketplace. Price: $0.003 per call. Blank values and the literal string 'null' are treated as unset. Invalid page, sort_by, price, product_condition or deal_type is a free 400 naming the parameter and the allowed values. Condition and deal refinements are per marketplace; a marketplace that lacks one gets the unfiltered feed plus an entry under filters_ignored, never a silent empty page. `product_num_ratings` is an integer; `offers_count` is the "N offers" count a result card shows, an integer, and null when the card shows none (most cards; it used to default to 1; "21+ used & new offers" reads 21); `product_minimum_offer_price` is the price on the card's "More Buying Choices" line -- the lowest among the listing's other offers, new or used -- a decimal string, null when the card shows no such line; under product_condition=USED the answer carries `price_note`, which says which price is which, and offers_stock with the USED_* conditions returns the used offers themselves; `product_brand` is the brand line Amazon prints above some titles (fashion and many branded listings) and null on cards without one -- product_details has `brand_name` for every ASIN; `product_star_rating`, `product_price` and `product_original_price` are decimal strings; a null field means Amazon did not show it. `is_prime` is true when the result carries a Prime badge or its delivery line offers Prime delivery. `metadata.reachable_pages` says how far `page` can go: Amazon serves at most 7 pages of a query even when `metadata.total_pages` counts more (then `pagination_note` says how to split the query). `metadata.next_page` is the page to ask for next (null on the last one) and `_links.next` its link; each row's `position` is its place on this page, from 1, sponsored rows counted as Amazon lists them; a page past the end is a free 400 `page_out_of_range`. A full page is up to 48 results and about 54 KB; the tool returns the first 10 as light rows by default and the answer carries `_truncated`, `_omitted_fields`, `_projection` and `_notes`. filters_applied echoes the effective sort_by (RELEVANCE when none was sent). A BEST_SELLERS ordering is Amazon's query-scoped popularity, not a category rank: a row's `badges` / `is_best_seller` are what the result card showed for this query, and an ASIN that is #1 in its subcategory can carry no badge here while product_details reports best_seller=true with the rank. For a rank claim, use product_details or best_sellers. An empty `products` list is served as success only when Amazon itself reports 0 results (metadata.total is 0 and `hint` says so). Anything else that is not a usable result is an unbilled, retryable 503 with code upstream_unavailable.

query.description: Search keywords. Required and must be non-empty.
query.title: Query

page.description: Result page, 1-based. metadata.total_pages says how far it goes.
page.title: Page

category_id.description: Amazon browse node id to restrict to, e.g. 172282 (Electronics on US). Take one from a best_sellers answer's available_subcategories, a product's category_path, or node= in an Amazon URL. Ids differ per marketplace.
category_id.title: Category Id

min_price.description: Lowest price, in the marketplace currency; decimals such as 19.99 are fine.
min_price.title: Min Price

max_price.description: Highest price, in the marketplace currency.
max_price.title: Max Price

product_condition.description: NEW, USED or RENEWED (case-insensitive). Applied with the marketplace's own condition node; where a marketplace does not offer one, the answer's filters_ignored says so and available_filters lists what it does offer. USED lists products that have a used offer: `product_price` stays the featured offer's price (usually a new item's) and `product_minimum_offer_price` is the lowest price among the listing's other offers.
product_condition.title: Product Condition

brand.description: Brand name as Amazon spells it (case-insensitive), e.g. Samsung.
brand.title: Brand

seller_id.description: Restrict results to one seller's offers: an Amazon seller id, 'A' followed by 9-20 letters and digits (e.g. A294P4X9EWVXLJ).
seller_id.title: Seller Id

today_deals.description: Only items in Today's Deals, using that marketplace's own refinement. Where a marketplace has none (amazon.fr on 2026-09-08) it is reported under filters_ignored.
today_deals.title: Today Deals

deal_type.description: A specific promotion refinement: today_deals, all_discounts, coupons or buy_more_save_more. available_filters.deal_type lists the ones this marketplace has.
deal_type.title: Deal Type

limit.description: How many search results to return from this page (0 = all of them). A full page is usually 48 rows (Amazon serves 16 to 60 depending on its layout; metadata.page_size says how many) and about 54 KB, which most clients spill to a file instead of showing inline. The answer carries _truncated with the true count when it trims.
limit.title: Limit

compact.description: Return light rows: identity, price, rating, badges and one delivery_date, dropping the long delivery prose that repeats itself across three fields. false returns every field the REST API sends (roughly 3x the size).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated row fields to return instead of the light set, e.g. "asin,product_title,product_price". Rows list what they left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: product_details_batch
tools.description: Use to enrich a list of ASINs in one call; compare the ASINs in `results` with the ones you sent. Batch variant of product_details. Accepts a comma-separated ASIN list, deduplicates it, and fetches all of them concurrently. Far cheaper and faster than N single calls. Price: $0.0024 per item (max 20). Billed per ASIN processed, including ones that come back not-found. More than 20 ASINs returns 413. Bullet points and specs are what Amazon shows for the listing; on multi-variant listings they can describe the product family rather than the exact variant. A null field means Amazon did not show it. ASINs Amazon has no record for on that marketplace are listed in not_returned (billed, like a not-found product_details call; retrying will not help). The batch record comes from Amazon's app, not the product page: price, rating, availability, images, bullets and variants, but no best-seller ranks, no best-seller badge, no category path and no merchant (seller) id (`is_best_seller` is false here whatever the product, because the source carries no badge, and is left out of the compact row). For those call product_details per ASIN. On an API key both cost one request per ASIN, so the batch saves calls and time, not money; keyless (x402) it is also cheaper per item. Compact rows carry brand, weight {raw, unit, value} and dimension {length, width, height, unit, raw} in product_details' shape, read from the row's product_attributes (package dimensions first); outside amazon.com Amazon's app prints centimetres under an inches label, so there dimension.unit is cm while raw keeps Amazon's text. Prices are decimal strings as each source prints them ("179.0" here, "179.00" on product_details): compare them as numbers.

asins.description: Comma-separated ASIN list, maximum 20 after de-duplication. Each must be 10 uppercase alphanumeric characters. An Amazon product URL (…/dp/ASIN) works too, in place of an ASIN; lower case is fine. A URL's domain sets the marketplace unless geo says otherwise.
asins.title: Asins

compact.description: Return the compact record (about 2-7 KB a row: title, brand, price, availability, rating summary, bullets, weight, dimension, variation_summary). false returns the full app record (15-150 KB a row: the product_attributes and product_details spec tables, images, the variation maps).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated top-level fields to return instead of the compact set, e.g. "weight,dimension,brand" or "product_attributes" (the whole spec table). Any response lists what it left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: offers_stock
tools.description: Use to compare sellers' current offers and see who holds the buy box, and, with check_inventory, how many units a buyer can add to the cart now. The stock number is not a sales estimate. Not for the listing's own details (product_details). Returns the current offer list per ASIN (seller, price, condition, buy-box winner) and, optionally, the actual purchasable stock quantity. The whole offer list comes by default; `page` returns it ten offers at a time. Price: $0.0045 per item (max 10). On an account, a call is billed per page of the offer list it delivers, plus the cart checks of check_inventory. Amazon lists ten offers a page, so an ASIN with up to ten offers is one request and each further page of its list is one more (a listing with 35 offers: 4). `page` (1, 2, ...) returns that page alone for one request per ASIN -- page 1 is the buy-box offer and the first ten of the list -- and each row then carries `page` and `total_pages`. A page past the end is answered like a not-found item: code `page_out_of_range`, billed, with `total_pages` and `offers_total` in the row; `total_pages` on any page says how far to go, so there is no need to ask. Without `page` the whole list comes, up to 10 pages (100 offers and the buy-box offer); a longer list says so in `coverage_note`, and `page=11` onward reaches the rest. `offers_total` is Amazon's own count of the offers under the condition filter, not the number returned; when fewer are returned, `coverage_note` says why (a page that could not be read this time, the 10-page limit, or offers that cannot be added to a cart). A condition filter covers the buy-box offer too: it is in the answer only when its own condition was asked for. offers_count=winner returns only the offer flagged is_buybox_winner (offers_total keeps the full count); it used to scope only the inventory check and return every offer. /scrape is a legacy alias for the same handler. When Amazon will not return the offer list for an ASIN, the result carries source=product_page: the featured (buy-box) offer read from the product page, offers_on_amazon (how many offers Amazon says exist) and a note; other sellers' offers and stock are then not included. With check_inventory, a cart check that cannot read a quantity is retried once on another session; one that still fails says so on the offer, inventory_response {"error": "cart check failed", "code": "cart_check_failed", "retryable": true}, is not billed, and never reads as a quantity of 0. An offer whose price Amazon shows only in the cart ("Add to cart to see product details") has `price` null and `price_hidden` true; it used to read as price 0. Each offer carries `ships_from` (the "Ships from" name: Amazon for FBA, else the seller), `delivery_message` (the offer's own delivery promise, e.g. "FREE delivery Friday, October 16 on orders shipped by Amazon over $35") and `delivery_message_secondary` (the "Or fastest delivery ..." line), null when the offer shows none. `delivery` is the same value as `ships_from`, kept for existing integrations; it never held delivery information. A row for an ASIN that could not be answered carries `error`, `code`, `http_status`, `billed`, `retryable` and `next_step`, like a top-level error: `upstream_unavailable` (not billed, retry that ASIN), `no_offers` ("No offers found": the offer list holds no offer that can be bought as is -- customizable listings have none; billed like a 404) or `asin_redirected` (Amazon answers the ASIN with another listing's offers; billed like a 404). On agent.apiguru.app the answer also carries `success` and `_links` (self, and `details_url` per row); `billable_requests_count` is there on your own key only. Each offer carries `merchant_id` and `sold_by_amazon`. Amazon lists its own offers (Amazon.com, Amazon Resale and their local names) without a seller link, so on those rows `seller_id` repeats the seller's name; `merchant_id` is the id to use: the linked seller's id, or for Amazon's own offers the merchant id the product page states (null when it states none). `sold_by_amazon` is true for Amazon's own offers, false for a linked seller and null when the row does not say. Amazon itself has no seller profile to look up.

asins.description: Comma-separated ASIN list, maximum 10. Each must be 10 uppercase alphanumeric characters; malformed entries are rejected with 400. An Amazon product URL (…/dp/ASIN) works too, in place of an ASIN; lower case is fine. A URL's domain sets the marketplace unless geo says otherwise.
asins.title: Asins

check_inventory.description: Add each offer's purchasable stock quantity (`inventory_response`), read with a cart check. Slower, and each check that reads a quantity is billed, so leave off unless you need the number.
check_inventory.title: Check Inventory

offers_count.description: 'all' for every offer (default), 'winner' for the buy-box offer only, or a specific alphanumeric Offer ID. Every offer carries is_buybox_winner; with 'winner' the per-ASIN data holds that one offer and offers_total says how many exist. An ASIN with no featured offer answers an empty list with an explanatory error. The response echoes filters_applied.
offers_count.title: Offers Count

condition.description: Comma-separated condition filter: ALL, NEW, USED_LIKE_NEW, USED_VERY_GOOD, USED_GOOD, USED_ACCEPTABLE (case-insensitive). Omit for every offer. The filter covers the buy-box offer too: it is in the answer only when its own condition is among those asked for. An unknown value is a free 400 listing the allowed ones; it used to be silently treated as ALL.
condition.title: Condition

page.description: One page of each ASIN's offer list instead of the whole list. Amazon lists ten offers a page, in its own order (it starts from the lowest price with delivery); page 1 also carries the buy-box offer. One request per ASIN whatever the listing's size, and each row then says `page` and `total_pages`. Omit for the whole list, which is one request per page of ten.
page.title: Page

tools.name: best_sellers
tools.description: Use for what sells best in a department right now. The rank is Amazon's, not a sales figure. Best-seller rankings for a department of one marketplace, 50 per page. Every answer carries the department it resolved to and how (category_resolution: by slug, name or a fragment of a name, with a hint when a fragment such as 'shoes' landed on the whole 'Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry' department, or 'subcategory' when a word such as 'camera' named a subcategory), available_categories (that marketplace's departments with slugs; MCP: with compact=false) and available_subcategories (the children of the node shown, with the ids subcategory_code takes). On amazon.com subcategory_code also takes any browse node id at any depth, or a name resolved under the department ("women's shoes", "mules & clogs"); category.subcategory_path gives the node's full path and category.heading the page's own title line. Price: $0.003 per call. No required parameters - calling it bare returns US appliances page 1. `category` accepts a slug, a display name, one of the older US department names, or a unique fragment; category_resolution.via says which, and a fragment match adds a hint naming the subcategories that carry the word, with ids. On amazon.com the whole browse tree is known: subcategory_code takes any node id or a name at any depth, subcategory_name and subcategory_path are filled without a fetch, and available_subcategories lists the node's real children (empty on a leaf). Other marketplaces name only what their navigation showed. page is capped at 5 (a 400 beyond, not a 500). `rank` is the position within the requested list on this page. Rows are the same for every marketplace; only the department vocabulary differs, and the answer carries it.

category.description: Best-seller department, by slug or by name as Amazon shows it for that marketplace (case-insensitive; a unique fragment works, and the answer's category_resolution says when a fragment was used -- 'shoes' is the whole 'Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry' department, and the hint then lists the Shoes subcategories with their ids). Departments and their slugs differ per marketplace: amazon.com has electronics, amazon.de has ce-de (Electronics & Photo). A word that names a subcategory works too: category=camera on amazon.es is Electronics > Camera & Photo (category_resolution.via says 'subcategory'; several equally good matches are a free 400 listing each as category + subcategory_code). REST answers list the marketplace's departments under available_categories (the MCP tool with compact=false); an unknown name is a free 400 listing them.
category.title: Category

subcategory_code.description: Browse node id under `category`: one from available_subcategories of a previous answer, or on amazon.com any node id at any depth (679410011 is Women > Shoes > Mules & Clogs) or a name resolved under the department ("women's shoes", "mens boots", "mules & clogs"). A name that fits two nodes equally (Men > Shoes > Boots and Women > Shoes > Boots) is a free 400 listing both ids with their paths.
subcategory_code.title: Subcategory Code

page.description: Result page, 1-based, 50 rows each; Amazon's lists stop at page 5.
page.title: Page

limit.description: How many ranked products to return from this page (0 = all of them). A full page is 50 rows, which most clients spill to a file instead of showing inline. The answer carries _truncated with the true count when it trims.
limit.title: Limit

compact.description: Return light rows: identity, price, rating, badges and one delivery_date, dropping the long delivery prose that repeats itself across three fields. false returns every field the REST API sends (roughly 3x the size).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated row fields to return instead of the light set, e.g. "asin,product_title,product_price". Rows list what they left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: deals
tools.description: Use for items currently promoted in Amazon's deals feed. Not for one product's price (product_details); for a brand by name use search with brand= and today_deals=true. Returns the current Amazon deals feed: ASIN, title, deal price, list price, discount, deal badge, start/end time and product links. Filter by department (categories), brand id (brands), rating cut-off, price bounds, minimum discount and Prime program. Every answer carries available_filters (the category and brand ids this marketplace accepts, with names), filters_applied / filters_ignored (what took effect) and next_offset (the next page, null when the feed ends). Price: $0.003 per call. Filters are by id: categories takes a department id or name, brands takes brand ids only; available_filters in every answer lists both with names, and filters_applied / filters_ignored report what Amazon honoured. A page is 30 rows; page with offset=next_offset (null when exhausted); total_count caps at 500. min_price, max_price, min_discount and max_discount are applied to the rows after retrieval, scanning up to 3 feed pages per call, so a page can hold fewer than 30 rows and total_count does not reflect them. An empty answer carries a hint saying why. Deal prices expire: check deal_ends_at. The older price_range and discount_range parameters are still accepted, as buckets (1-5 = under 25 / 25-50 / 50-100 / 100-200 / 200 and up; 1-4 = 10 / 25 / 50 / 70 percent off or more) or as bands such as 25-50 and 70+. `discount_percentage` is Amazon's display string ("18%") and `discount_absolute` a decimal string; on product_details `discount_percentage` is a number.

offset.description: Row to start at. A page is 30 rows; pass the previous answer's next_offset for the next page.
offset.title: Offset

categories.description: Department to restrict to: its id from available_filters.categories, or its name as Amazon shows it for that marketplace (case-insensitive; a unique fragment such as "electronics" works). US departments: Amazon Devices & Accessories, Appliances, Arts Crafts & Sewing, Audible Books & Originals, Automotive, Baby Products, Beauty & Personal Care, Books, CDs & Vinyl, Cell Phones & Accessories, Clothing Shoes & Jewelry, Collectibles & Fine Art, Electronics, Everything Else, Grocery & Gourmet Food, Handmade Products, Health & Household, Home & Kitchen, Industrial & Scientific, Kindle Store, Movies & TV, Musical Instruments, Office Products, Patio Lawn & Garden, Pet Supplies, Software, Sports & Outdoors, Tools & Home Improvement, Toys & Games, Video Games. Other marketplaces use their own localised names -- read them from available_filters.categories of any deals answer for that geo. An unknown name is a free 400 listing the valid names.
categories.title: Categories

brands.description: Comma-separated brand ids, e.g. 46655 for Samsung on US. Take them from brand_id on any deals row or from available_filters.brands (the brands present in the current result). Names resolve only when this marketplace has already shown that brand; for a brand by name use /search with brand=<name> and today_deals=true instead.
brands.title: Brands

min_product_star_rating.description: Amazon's deals feed offers one rating cut-off: 4 = four stars and up. ALL or omitted = no cut-off. Other values are rejected with a free 400.
min_product_star_rating.title: Min Product Star Rating

min_price.description: Lowest deal price to return, in the marketplace currency. Applied to the fetched rows; see notes.
min_price.title: Min Price

max_price.description: Highest deal price to return, in the marketplace currency.
max_price.title: Max Price

min_discount.description: Smallest discount percentage to return, e.g. 50 for half price or better.
min_discount.title: Min Discount

prime_exclusive.description: Only deals in Amazon's Prime Exclusive program.
prime_exclusive.title: Prime Exclusive

prime_early_access.description: Only Prime Early Access deals. A marketplace lists the programs it is running under available_filters.prime_programs; when Early Access is not running the answer is empty with a hint saying so.
prime_early_access.title: Prime Early Access

limit.description: How many deals to return from this page (0 = all of them). A full page is 30 rows and roughly 35 KB with every field, which most clients spill to a file instead of showing inline. The answer carries _truncated with the true count when it trims.
limit.title: Limit

compact.description: Return light rows: identity, prices, discount, badge, end time, links, brand_id and department_ids, dropping the image arrays. false returns every field the REST API sends.
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated row fields to return instead of the light set, e.g. "asin,product_title,product_price". Rows list what they left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: seller_profile_batch
tools.description: Use to vet sellers: name, rating and feedback counts as Amazon displays them. Returns the storefront profile for each seller id: business name, rating, feedback counts, address and marketplace presence. Price: $0.0036 per item (max 10). Seller ID validation is all-or-nothing: one malformed id rejects the entire request with 400. Every row in results is an object with `status`: `ok` (the profile), `not_found` (Amazon has no page for that id on this marketplace; billed, like a 404) or `unavailable` (could not be retrieved right now; NOT billed on the keyed path, `retryable: true`). A row is never null. billable_requests_count counts ok + not_found rows; on the pay-per-call rail the per-item quote is settled up front, so retry `unavailable` ids in a separate call rather than expecting a partial refund. On agent.apiguru.app the answer also carries `success` and `_links.self`; `billable_requests_count` is there on your own key only. Amazon itself has no seller profile: the merchant id of an offer sold by Amazon (offers_stock marks those `sold_by_amazon`) answers `not_found`, billed like any other.

seller_ids.description: Comma-separated seller IDs, maximum 10. Each must be an Amazon seller id -- 'A' followed by 9-20 letters and digits, e.g. A294P4X9EWVXLJ -- or the whole call 400s.
seller_ids.title: Seller Ids

tools.name: seller_products
tools.description: Use to list one seller's storefront. Products listed by a seller: a storefront search. Takes the same filters as search -- query, page, sort_by, category_id, min_price / max_price, product_condition, brand, today_deals, deal_type -- and answers with filters_applied, filters_ignored and available_filters like search does. Price: $0.003 per call. A malformed seller_id is a free 400, as on seller_profile_batch. metadata.total_pages counts every page of the result (48 rows a page), but Amazon serves at most 7 pages of one query: metadata.reachable_pages is how far page can go, and when it is less, pagination_note says how to see the rest (min_price/max_price bands or category_id). _links.next is the next page while there is one; a page past the end is a free 400 page_out_of_range. Invalid sort_by, price, product_condition or deal_type is a free 400 that lists the allowed values. No single sort order lists a whole storefront: Amazon's relevance order (the default) can count far fewer products than the store holds and repeats products across pages, and other orders include products it leaves out (measured on one store: relevance 321, NEWEST 1,898; on another, relevance and NEWEST shared 90 of 161 products). Page 1 of a storefront without `query` carries `coverage_note` with the recipe: page through sort_by=RELEVANCE and sort_by=NEWEST, split a store larger than 336 products into min_price/max_price bands, dedupe by asin. An empty storefront carries `note`: Amazon reports 0 products for a seller with no listings on that marketplace and for an id that is not a seller alike, so check it with seller_profile_batch (`_links.seller_profile`). Rows have the search row shape: `offers_count` is null unless the card shows a count, and `product_brand` is null on most storefront cards (Amazon prints no brand line there; product_details has `brand_name`). Rows carry `position` (their place on this page, from 1) and metadata carries `next_page`, as on search.

seller_id.description: Amazon seller id whose storefront to list: 'A' followed by 9-20 letters and digits, the seller= or me= value of a storefront URL (e.g. A294P4X9EWVXLJ). Required.
seller_id.title: Seller Id

query.description: Optional keywords to search within this seller's storefront.
query.title: Query

page.description: Result page, 1-based. metadata.total_pages says how far it goes.
page.title: Page

category_id.description: Amazon browse node id to restrict to, e.g. 172282 (Electronics on US). Take one from a best_sellers answer's available_subcategories, a product's category_path, or node= in an Amazon URL. Ids differ per marketplace.
category_id.title: Category Id

min_price.description: Lowest price, in the marketplace currency; decimals such as 19.99 are fine.
min_price.title: Min Price

max_price.description: Highest price, in the marketplace currency.
max_price.title: Max Price

product_condition.description: NEW, USED or RENEWED (case-insensitive). Applied with the marketplace's own condition node; where a marketplace does not offer one, the answer's filters_ignored says so and available_filters lists what it does offer.
product_condition.title: Product Condition

brand.description: Brand name as Amazon spells it (case-insensitive), e.g. Samsung.
brand.title: Brand

today_deals.description: Only items in Today's Deals, using that marketplace's own refinement. Where a marketplace has none (amazon.fr on 2026-09-08) it is reported under filters_ignored.
today_deals.title: Today Deals

deal_type.description: A specific promotion refinement: today_deals, all_discounts, coupons or buy_more_save_more. available_filters.deal_type lists the ones this marketplace has.
deal_type.title: Deal Type

limit.description: How many the seller's products to return from this page (0 = all of them). A full page is usually 48 rows (Amazon serves 16 to 60 depending on its layout; metadata.page_size says how many) and about 54 KB, which most clients spill to a file instead of showing inline. The answer carries _truncated with the true count when it trims.
limit.title: Limit

compact.description: Return light rows: identity, price, rating, badges and one delivery_date, dropping the long delivery prose that repeats itself across three fields. false returns every field the REST API sends (roughly 3x the size).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated row fields to return instead of the light set, e.g. "asin,product_title,product_price". Rows list what they left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: seller_reviews
tools.description: Use for a seller's customer feedback (service, shipping). Not for product reviews (product_reviews). Returns paginated seller feedback, optionally filtered to a star-rating window. Price: $0.003 per call. from_rating and to_rating are optional; omit both for unfiltered feedback. A page holds 5 reviews and the answer carries current_page and has_next_page; Amazon exposes no total, so page until has_next_page is false (up to page 100). Each review has `rater`, `rating`, `review_text`, `review_date` and, where the seller answered, `response_text`. `has_feedback` is Amazon's own flag for whether the seller has any feedback entry: a seller can have rating counts in the profile and none, and page 1 then carries a `note` saying so.

seller_id.description: Amazon seller id: 'A' followed by 9-20 letters and digits, the seller= or me= value of a storefront URL (e.g. A294P4X9EWVXLJ). Required.
seller_id.title: Seller Id

page.description: Result page, 1-based, 5 reviews a page; has_next_page in the answer says whether another exists.
page.title: Page

limit.description: How many seller reviews to return from this page (0 = all of them). A page holds 5 reviews. The answer carries _truncated with the true count when it trims.
limit.title: Limit

compact.description: Return light rows: identity, price, rating, badges and one delivery_date, dropping the long delivery prose that repeats itself across three fields. false returns every field the REST API sends (roughly 3x the size).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated row fields to return instead of the light set, e.g. "asin,product_title,product_price". Rows list what they left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description:
List every Apiguru endpoint with its price, required parameters and
        supported marketplaces, plus your current access mode and cache.
        Free: answers locally with no network request and no charge. Call
        this before paid tools if you need to plan.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description:
Report a bug, ask for a field, or say what would make this API more
        useful. Free: never billed, no API key needed.

        Prefer GitHub if you have an account -- an issue at
        https://github.com/apiguru-app/agent-kit/issues gets a reply on the
        thread, this wall does not. Use this tool when you have no GitHub
        account or nothing to attach one to.

        message:  what happened or what you want. Be specific: the tool, the
                  parameters, the field, what you expected, what you got, and
                  the request_id from the answer. One issue per entry -- a
                  five-point list cannot be closed point by point.
        category: bug | wish | praise | question | other
        endpoint: which tool or path it is about, e.g. "search".
        agent:    what you are, e.g. "acme-pricing-bot/2.1". Optional.
        contact:  a GitHub handle or email if you want a reply. Shown
                  publicly on the wall. Optional.
